messages:
Mira (customer-success): FYI Thalassa is reporting ~30% request error rate (503) from the hosted inference endpoint. They flagged potential SLA breach. Can someone own triage + immediate workaround?
Alex (eng-platform): On it. Any recent deploys to that model route?
Mira (customer-success): No customer-facing deploys. They saw spike at ~14:05 UTC. Sending logs and a short repro.
Mira (customer-success): ```
Request sample: POST /v1/generate model=redwood-4x
Headers: x-customer-id: thalassa
Response: 503 Service Unavailable - kv cache miss overflow
Latency: 1200ms
```
Jin (eng-oncall): I see alerts for pool-edge-7. I'm attaching incident id INC-2026-1147. ops-bot, can you put this into the incident channel and page the SRE rota? :rotating_light:
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1147 — severity=P1 — affected=hosted-regional-us-west-2 — pager=eng-sre. Link: https://incident.redwood/in/INC-2026-1147
Sam (eng-sre): Paging in. Quick hypothesis: KV cache backing store got pressure due to a burst of long-context requests. Short-term workaround: reduce max_context on the route and fallback to the smaller quantized variant for Thalassa.
Alex (eng-platform): Agreed. I can push a route policy override for thalassa to:
```yaml
route_overrides:
  thalassa:
    model_priority: [redwood-3q, redwood-4x]
    max_context: 1024
    max_concurrency: 10
```
I'll deploy the override as a canary to 10% in 10m.
Jin (eng-oncall): Please also add a temporary burst capacity from Dedicated pool if available — customer is on committed plan and that buys us time. Sam, can you open runbook ticket and check eviction logs?
Sam (eng-sre): Opening runbook now -> https://tickets.redwood/r/3421. Eviction logs show repeated KV cache OOMs at 14:04:23. We'll increase cache TTL and throttle long-tail requests in the router for 15m.
Mira (customer-success): Thanks. Thalassa asks for ETA on a fix and whether they'll need to change their request patterns.
Alex (eng-platform): ETA: I'll have the route override rolled out to 10% within 20m, monitor p50/p99 and error rate. If stable, promote to 100% in 45-60m. Short ask to the customer: avoid 16k+ context requests for next 1 hour if possible. I'll post the canary status here.
Jin (eng-oncall): I'll update incident notes and set the SLO status to "at risk". Sam will continue to look at infra side.
Sam (eng-sre): If the override doesn't help, plan B is an emergency fallback to redwood-3q (lower mem) and a temporary increase in dedicated capacity. I can author the infra change; need a +1 from Alex for routing changes.
Alex (eng-platform): +1 for plan B. Also creating a PR for the rollback safety check: https://git.redwood/p/routing/PR-987.
Mira (customer-success): Appreciate the fast responses. Please ping me when canary hits 0 errors for 10m so I can update the customer.
Jin (eng-oncall): Noted. I'll post back status updates every 10m and close the loop when the error rate is <1% for 15m.
Alex (eng-platform): Canary deployed to 10% at 14:22 UTC. Monitoring.
Sam (eng-sre): Adjusted cache TTL + temporary router throttle in place. Watching for regressions.
ops-bot: Pager acknowledged by Sam (eng-sre) and Jin (eng-oncall).
Mira (customer-success): Thanks team. If anything changes with the SLA timeline I'll escalate to sales ops. :thumbsup:
